zh: 自从罗四姐嫁到到胡家，真是走了一步帮夫运，胡雪岩的事业如《红楼梦》上所形容的“鲜花着锦”般兴旺。当然，兴旺的由来是他恃左宗棠为靠山，左宗棠视他为股肽，只要左宗棠西征，节节胜利，所请在朝廷无有不准，胡雪岩水涨船高，亦就事事顺手了。原来从道光年问开始，君暗臣愚，激出内忧外患，西北的回民起义，亦是贪官污吏激荡而成。其时所谓“甘回”共有西、南北三大支，三大首领，西面的叫马朵之，驻扎在青海的西宁，南面的叫马占鳌，以甘肃与青海的河州，也就是临夏为根据地，北面叫马化龙，是三大首领中最厉害的一个，势力范围在宁夏、灵武一带，根据地名为金积堡，这个地方就是“黄河百害，惟富一套”的河套的起点，擅茶、马之利以外，东面有个盐池叫花马池，更是一大财源。金积堡周围有五百多个寨子，众星拱月般环卫着马化龙的金积堡。此人对宁夏将军穆图善很恭敬。左宗棠看到了此人的底蕴，所以西征的第一目标就是攻下金积堡。
en: Once Luo Sijie married into the Hu household, she truly entered upon a fortune that advanced her husband. Hu Xueyan's enterprises flourished like “fresh flowers upon brocade,” as Dream of the Red Chamber puts it. Their prosperity, of course, rested on Zuo Zongtang's support, while Zuo regarded Hu as his indispensable right hand. As the western campaign advanced from victory to victory and the court granted every request Zuo made, Hu rose with the tide and found everything going smoothly. Since the Daoguang reign, benighted rulers and foolish ministers had provoked troubles at home and abroad. The Muslim uprisings in the northwest had likewise been stirred up by corrupt officials. The forces then known as the Gansu Muslims fell into three main divisions, western, southern and northern, with three principal leaders. In the west was Ma Duozhi, based at Xining in Qinghai. In the south was Ma Zhan'ao, whose base was Hezhou, also called Linxia, in the Gansu–Qinghai region. The northern leader, Ma Hualong, was the most formidable of the three. His influence extended over Ningxia and Lingwu, and his stronghold was Jinjibao. It stood at the beginning of the Hetao region, the great bend of the Yellow River celebrated in the saying, “The Yellow River brings a hundred troubles; only its bend grows rich.” Besides controlling the profits from tea and horses, he had a major source of wealth in Huamachi, a salt lake to the east. More than five hundred fortified villages encircled Jinjibao like stars surrounding the moon. Ma was extremely respectful towards Mutushan, the general at Ningxia. Zuo saw what lay beneath this behaviour, and the first objective of his western campaign was to capture Jinjibao.

zh: 在攻金积堡之前，先要隔断捻军与甘回的联系。捻军分为两大股，称为“东捻”、“西捻”。曾国藩解释捻军之捻说：“捻纸燃脂，故谓之捻”，凡是用薄纸搓成条状，如吸水烟用的纸煤等等，都叫做捻子。捻军的特性在于易聚易散，但看起来象乌合之众，而流转不定，飘忽千里，令人疲于奔命，亦很厉害。僧格林沁的黑龙江马队，追奔逐北，捻军见了就澈，但一停下来，周围不知如何，就会冒出无数捻军来，僧王就是这样阵亡的。僧王打的是东捻，西捻的首领叫张宗禹，自河南至陕西，由河南横渡黄河，直上延安、米脂，南北战线拉长到一千多里，目的就是希望与马化友由西往东，也有千把里的这条战线交会。只要一接上头，西捻不复可制，回民起义亦不知何时才能镇压下去，所以左宗棠西征的初步战略，就在隔离西捻与甘回不让他们“会师”。罗四姐嫁到胡家时，正当西捻初平，两宫太后召见左宗棠，天语褒嘉，左宗棠自陈五年可以镇压回民起义之时。
en: Before attacking Jinjibao, however, he had to sever the link between the Nian armies and the Gansu Muslim forces. The Nian were divided into two main groups, the Eastern and Western Nian. Explaining their name, Zeng Guofan wrote, “Paper is twisted to burn in oil; hence the name nian.” Anything made by twisting thin paper into a strip, such as the spills used for lighting water pipes, was called a nianzi. The Nian armies could gather and disperse with equal ease. Though they looked like an undisciplined rabble, their unpredictable movements over a thousand li left pursuers exhausted and made them formidable opponents. Sengge Rinchen's Heilongjiang cavalry chased them relentlessly. Whenever they saw it coming, they withdrew. Yet as soon as the cavalry halted, innumerable Nian soldiers would somehow appear all around it. That was how Prince Sengge Rinchen had met his death. He had been fighting the Eastern Nian. Zhang Zongyu, leader of the Western Nian, moved between Henan and Shaanxi, crossing the Yellow River from Henan and pressing north towards Yan'an and Mizhi. His north–south front stretched over a thousand li. He hoped to join Ma Hualong's front, which extended a similar distance from west to east. Once the two linked up, the Western Nian would be beyond control, and there would be no telling when the Muslim uprising could be suppressed. Zuo's initial strategy was therefore to keep them apart and prevent a junction. When Luo married into Hu's household, the Western Nian had just been defeated. The two empress dowagers received Zuo with gracious praise, and he declared that he could suppress the Muslim uprising within five years.

zh: 左宗棠最初驻军西安，然后往西北逐步推进，大营先移乾州，再移甘肃境内的泾川，然后往北打，攻克镇原、庆阳，收容降众及饥民十七万人，行屯垦之法，种子、农具，都由胡雪岩的转运局采办好了，运到甘肃。及至左宗棠的前锋逼进灵武，马化龙看根据地有被剿之虞，于是“上书言抚”，抚是安抚，表示愿意投降，部众或者收编为清军、或者遗散、或者为他们谋个生计。有此化干戈为玉帛的结果，本来是最理想的办法，但造反起义的，就抚而又反复音，不知多少。左宗棠阅历极丰，而马化友又有善于翻覆的名声，他可以玩弄穆图善，而左宗棠决不会受他的愚，所以置之不理，备妥三月行粮，进攻金积堡。
en: Zuo first stationed his army at Xi'an, then advanced gradually northwest. Headquarters moved first to Qianzhou, then to Jingchuan in Gansu. Turning north, he captured Zhenyuan and Qingyang, took in 170,000 surrendered people and famine refugees, and established agricultural settlements for them. The seeds and farming implements were all procured by Hu's Transport Bureau and shipped to Gansu. When Zuo's advance troops approached Lingwu, Ma Hualong saw that his base was in danger of destruction and submitted a letter asking for pacification. That meant he was willing to surrender: his followers might be absorbed into the Qing army, dispersed, or provided with some means of livelihood. Turning weapons into peaceful relations would have been the ideal outcome. But countless rebels had accepted pacification only to rise again. Zuo was deeply experienced, and Ma had a reputation for repeated reversals. He might play tricks on Mutushan, but Zuo would not be fooled. Ignoring the appeal, he prepared three months' provisions and advanced on Jinjibao.

zh: 指挥此役的大将是刘松山。此人是曾国藩的小同乡，行伍出身，积功升至总兵。咸丰十年，英法内犯，僧格林沁提兵勤王，东南没有这一支膘悍的马队，战局大受影响。那时太平军李秀成，刚开始为洪秀全所重用，在芜湖召集军事会议，分道进兵，李秀成本人自率大军，由芜湖南下，攻占皖南黟县，另外太平军悍将李世贤、黄文金、李继远等，相继陷宁国、下徽州，又占江西浮梁、都昌、饶州。驻节祁门的曾国藩，西面来自湖北的接济，因江西粮道中断而绝，东面则有二李亲领的骄兵相逼，重重围困，听从幕宾建议，反攻徽州，以期打开通浙江的运道。于是曾国藩侈军祁门以东、徽州以西的休宁；有一天太平军夜袭，诸营皆贵，只有刘松山在月下列队迎敌，太平军不敢相逼，其余溃散各营，月夜看不真切，以为太平军拦截，掉头要逃，及至刘松山打出真号，大家才知道大营未夫，“老帅”无恙，惊魂始定。祁门一役，是曾国藩靖港兵败，投水遇救以后，另一次的大危机，他连遗书都写好了，结果转危为安，都由刘松山之功，从此以国士相待。
en: The general commanding the attack was Liu Songshan, a man from Zeng Guofan's own immediate home district. He had risen from the ranks to become a brigade commander through distinguished service. In the tenth year of Xianfeng, when British and French forces invaded, Sengge Rinchen had taken his troops to defend the emperor. The removal of that fierce cavalry force from the southeast greatly affected the war there. Li Xiucheng, just beginning to enjoy Hong Xiuquan's confidence, convened a military conference at Wuhu and divided the Taiping forces for an advance on several routes. He himself marched south from Wuhu and captured Yi County in southern Anhui. Other formidable Taiping commanders, Li Shixian, Huang Wenjin and Li Jiyuan, successively took Ningguo and Huizhou, followed by Fuliang, Duchang and Raozhou in Jiangxi. Zeng, based at Qimen, was cut off from his Hubei supplies to the west because the route through Jiangxi had been broken. From the east, confident troops led personally by the two Lis pressed upon him. Encircled, he accepted his advisers' proposal to counterattack Huizhou and reopen a supply route to Zhejiang. He therefore moved his army to Xiuning, east of Qimen and west of Huizhou. One night the Taipings attacked, and every camp broke except Liu's. Liu formed his men in the moonlight to meet the enemy, who dared not approach. Troops fleeing from the other camps, unable to see clearly, mistook his ranks for a Taiping blocking force and turned to run. Only when Liu displayed the proper recognition signals did they realize that headquarters still held and the old commander was safe. Their terror subsided. Since his defeat at Jinggang, when he had thrown himself into the water and been rescued, this had been Zeng's next great crisis. He had even written his last letters. His escape was entirely due to Liu, whom he thereafter treated as a man of exceptional national worth.

zh: 及至左宗棠受命西征，这是一场大战役，非地方性的军务可比，各军理当协力，曾国藩将他最重视的刘松山一军，交给左宗棠指挥。左宗棠本由曾国藩所提携，以后由于争饷而存意见，复以曾国荃破金陵，纵容洪秀全之子逃遁，直言讦奏，因而失和，不通音问已久，到这时，左宗棠才知道，谋国之忠，知人之明，自愧不如元辅“。将刘松山一军交他节制，比作曾国藩”嫁女“，对刘讼山的重用，自不待言。刘松山真亦不负曾国藩的知遇及左宗棠的期许，打西捻、甘回，几乎战无不胜、攻无不克。他从军以前，在家乡就已定下亲事，聘而未娶，在军中十几年，只因招兵，回过一次家乡，直到西捻既败，方在洛阳成婚，新郎新娘都三十多岁了。蜜月只得十天，刘松山便即入陕，肃清榆、延、绥、鄜四州以后，进军灵武，一战而克。马化龙力战无功，一面再次言抚，一面四处求援，但西宁、河州、临洮、靖远各地的回民军，震于刘松山的威名，都不敢妄运，于是刘松山大举进攻。同治九年正月，攻金积堡外围一个寨子，中炮坠马，因而阵亡，所部由他的侄子刘锦棠率领，同年十一月，终于攻克了金积堡。
en: When Zuo received command of the western expedition, its scale demanded cooperation from all the armies; this was no merely local operation. Zeng placed his most valued force, Liu Songshan's, under Zuo's command. Zuo had originally owed his advancement to Zeng, but they had later quarrelled over military funds. When Zeng Guoquan captured Jinling and allowed Hong Xiuquan's son to escape, Zuo openly denounced the matter in a memorial. Their relations broke down, and they had long ceased corresponding. Only now did Zuo acknowledge, “In loyalty to the country's interests and discernment of men, I am ashamed to fall short of the Grand Secretary.” He compared Zeng's placing Liu under his orders to giving a daughter in marriage. Needless to say, he entrusted Liu with important duties. Liu fully justified both Zeng's recognition and Zuo's expectations, winning almost every engagement against the Western Nian and the Gansu Muslim forces. Before enlisting, he had become engaged at home but had not married. In more than ten years of service, he returned home only once, to recruit men. Not until the Western Nian were defeated did he finally marry at Luoyang. Bride and groom were both over thirty. After a honeymoon of only ten days, he entered Shaanxi. Clearing the four districts of Yu, Yan, Sui and Fu, he advanced on Lingwu and took it in a single battle. Unable to defeat him, Ma Hualong again sought pacification while appealing everywhere for help. But the Muslim armies at Xining, Hezhou, Lintao and Jingyuan, overawed by Liu's reputation, dared not move rashly. Liu launched a major assault. In the first lunar month of the ninth year of Tongzhi, he was struck by cannon fire while attacking a fortified village outside Jinjibao, fell from his horse and died. His nephew Liu Jintang took command. In the eleventh month of that same year, Jinjibao finally fell.

zh: 西征军能够胜多败少，着着进展，是因为器械利、士气旺、纪律好。胡雪岩得古应春之力，西洋凡有新式枪械，以及其他精巧的军事装备，只要能用得上的，不必向左宗棠请示，先就办了来，加以补给适时，从无粮饷不断之虞，士气自然就旺盛了。这是西征军将士都佩服，也感激胡雪岩的，但纪律好亦应归功于胡雪岩，就只有左宗棠最明白了。从成丰未年，同治皇后阿鲁待氏的祖父赛尚武丧师失律，浪掷了一笔发自部库的二百万两银子的军饷以后，仗都是地方上自己在打，因此有楚军、湘军、淮军、浙军、粤军等等名号，都称之为“官军”，这些官军，来源不一，“回乡招募”的子弟兵固占多数，但也不个是土匪或者别处投过来的，出身不同，队官的作风各异，军纪就大有区别。湘军中以彭玉鳞部下纪律最严，鲍超一军最糟糕，这就是带兵的看法不同之故，不过鲍超骁勇善战，是曾国藩的“爱将”，所以诸事宽容。左宗棠所部，亦是杂牌军队，但都能格守纪律，一半是左宗棠治军较严，一半亦由于心悦诚服，不忍违犯纪律，论心悦诚服之所起，就不能不推服胡雪岩了，“湖湘子弟满天下”而无后顾之忧，都由于胡雪岩靠他广设钱庄、通汇便利，按时得能接济官兵家属。至于阵亡将士，恤死养生，不用左宗棠关照，他就派人去做了，大家都道“侯爷”如此爱护部下，何忍犯他的军纪？却不知是胡雪岩在助“候爷”维持纪律。
en: The western army won more often than it lost and advanced steadily because its weapons were superior, its morale high and its discipline good. With Gu Yingchun's help, Hu bought any new Western firearms or ingenious military equipment that could be useful, without first asking Zuo for instructions. Supplies arrived on time; the troops never feared an interruption in provisions or pay. Naturally, morale was high. Officers and men admired Hu for this and were grateful. But only Zuo fully understood that their discipline too owed much to him. Since the closing years of Xianfeng, when Saishang’a, grandfather of the Tongzhi emperor's empress of the Aludai clan, had lost his army and squandered two million taels of military funds from the ministry treasury, the provinces had been fighting their own wars. Hence the various Chu, Hunan, Huai, Zhejiang and Guangdong armies, all called government troops. They came from many sources. Men recruited in their commanders' home districts formed the majority, but there were also bandits and men transferred from elsewhere. Their backgrounds differed, as did their officers' methods, and discipline varied greatly. Within the Hunan Army, Peng Yulin's men were the best disciplined and Bao Chao's the worst, reflecting their commanders' differing views. But Bao was brave and skilful, a favourite of Zeng's, and was indulged in many things. Zuo's forces were equally mixed, yet they all observed discipline. Half the credit belonged to his strict command; the other half to their wholehearted devotion, which made them unwilling to disobey. For that devotion, Hu deserved acknowledgement. Hunan men served all over the empire without anxiety for those at home because his extensive network of banks and convenient remittances supported their families regularly. When officers or soldiers died, he sent men to provide death benefits and support the survivors without waiting for Zuo's instructions. Everyone thought: the marquis cares so much for us; how could we bear to violate his discipline? They did not know that Hu was helping the marquis maintain it.

zh: 胡雪岩能够公私兼顾，钱庄。典当、丝号一家接一家开张，生意越做越大，“财神”的名气越来越响，从胡老太太起始，都认为是“螺蛳太太”的功劳，原来为了避免用“二太太”之名，却又想不出更合适的称呼，有个通人说：“顺治年间‘江左三大家’之一的龚芝麓，娶了秦淮出身的顾眉生，龚芝麓的元配称她为‘顾太太’，仿照这个例子，拿‘罗四姐，的’姐，字改为‘太太’，有何不可？于是，‘罗四太太，就此叫开了。下人不明其理，只当她娘家住在螺蛳门外的缘故，叫成’螺蛳太太“。但最为乡党称道，而且使得胡雪岩自觉对螺蛳太太有愧，既爱且敬的是，她有个“大贤大德”的名声，为胡雪岩娶了十一房姨太太。
en: Hu managed to attend to public duties and private business alike. Banks, pawnshops and silk firms opened one after another, his enterprises expanded, and his reputation as the God of Wealth grew ever louder. Everyone, beginning with Old Madam Hu, attributed it to Madam Luosi. That title had arisen because they wished to avoid calling her Second Madam but could think of nothing more suitable. A learned man had offered a precedent: “In the Shunzhi reign, Gong Zhilu, one of the Three Great Masters of the Lower Yangtze, married Gu Meisheng, who came from the Qinhuai courtesan quarter. Gong's principal wife addressed her as Madam Gu. Why not follow that example and replace the ‘Sister’ in ‘Luo Sijie’ with ‘Madam’?” Thus she became Madam Luo Si. Servants who did not understand the reasoning assumed the title came from her family home outside Luosi, or Snail, Gate, and it became Madam Luosi. What most impressed their neighbours, however, and made Hu feel indebted to her, loving and respecting her all the more, was her reputation for extraordinary virtue: she arranged for him to take eleven more concubines.

zh: 约莫嫁后一年，螺蛳太太向到杭州三天竺来烧香的七姑奶奶诉苦。原来胡雪岩精力过人，只她一个人“当夕”，有些力不从心，因而也就觉得乐不敌苦了。于是胡雪岩不免留连花丛，本来欢场中应酬，在胡雪岩几乎是每天的例课，以前仅止于“吃花酒”，渐渐地以勾栏为行馆，经常整夜不归，其至在“堂子”里接见宾客，料理公事，这件事就可忧了。“七姐，”螺蛳太太说：“他现在正在风头上，这步桃花运走不得，第一，伤身体，第二，耽误正事，第三，名声不好听，还有第四，伙计们看东家的样，个个狂嫖滥赌，怎么得了？就算不学他的样，也会灰心，辛辛苦苦帮他创业，哪知道他是这样子不成材！”七姑奶奶知道最后两句话，是她“夫子自道”的牢骚，不过，她也有些怀疑，“小爷叔对这个‘色，字看不破，是大家都晓得的。不过，”她问；“又何至于’好‘到这个程度呢？”“喏，”螺蛳太太不免有怨言，“都是我们那位刘三叔！”
en: About a year after her marriage, Madam Luosi confided her troubles to the Seventh Lady, who had come to Hangzhou to offer incense at the Three Tianzhu Temples. Hu had exceptional sexual energy. Being his sole nightly companion had become more than she could manage, and the pleasure no longer outweighed the strain. Hu consequently began lingering among the courtesans. Entertaining at their houses had long been an almost daily duty for him, but previously he had confined himself to dining and drinking there. Gradually he began treating the brothels as residences, frequently staying all night and even receiving visitors and transacting official business there. That was cause for concern. “Seventh Sister, he is riding high now. He cannot afford this run of romantic adventures. First, it harms his health. Second, it delays important business. Third, it damages his reputation. And fourth, what if every employee follows his example, whoring and gambling without restraint? Even if they don't imitate him, they will be discouraged. They work so hard to help him build his enterprises, only to discover that he is such a disappointment.” The Seventh Lady knew that these last words expressed her friend's own resentment. Still, she was puzzled. “Everyone knows that Little Uncle has never overcome his weakness for women. But why should it have reached such a degree?” Madam Luosi could not suppress a complaint. “It is all the fault of our Third Uncle Liu!”

zh: 原来胡雪岩决定开办药店，他本早有此心，恰好又受了气，去年夏天胡老大大受暑发痧，土法子是拿铜钱刮瘀，刮出一条鲜红的血痕，病势顿去。胡老太太的痧刮得很透，本来已经不要紧了，只是胡雪岩不放心，请“郎中”来看了以后，开方打药，一再关照下人要快！仍旧去了两个时辰才回来，胡雪岩对有关老母的事异常认真，当下大发了一场难得一见的脾气。下人等他骂完，方始声诉：原来这年时疫流行，打药的人排着队等，一等等了个把时辰，他忍不住挤上前去，象看病“拔号”似的，要求先配他的方子。“请你快点。我们老太太等在那里要吃呢！”“哪家没有老太太？”药店伙计答说：“你要快，不会自家去开一爿药店？”挨了骂的那人，一股怨气发泄在药店伙计头上，加油添酱地形容了一番，将胡雪岩的火气挑拨了起来，当时顿一顿足说：“好！我就开一爿给他看。”于是刘不才受命筹备，即日北上到直隶去采办药材，顺便带回来几百帖“狗皮膏药”，供胡雪岩试用。
en: Hu had decided to open a medicine shop. He had long wished to do so, and an affront had finally prompted him. The previous summer, his mother had suffered an attack of sha after exposure to the heat. The traditional remedy was to scrape the skin with a copper coin, producing a bright red streak, after which the symptoms promptly subsided. Old Madam Hu had been thoroughly scraped and was already out of danger, but her son remained anxious. He sent for a physician, then had the prescription taken to be made up, repeatedly telling the servant to hurry. Even so, the man did not return for two double-hours. Hu was exceptionally particular about anything concerning his mother, and he flew into one of his rare tempers. Only after the scolding ended did the servant explain. An epidemic was spreading that year, and customers had to queue for medicines. After waiting for more than a double-hour, he had lost patience and squeezed to the front, hoping to have his prescription filled out of turn, as people sometimes did when seeking a consultation. “Please hurry. Our old lady is waiting to take it.” “Who doesn't have an old lady at home?” the shop assistant replied. “If you are in such a hurry, why don't you open your own medicine shop?” The scolded servant now vented his resentment on the assistant, embellishing the account until he rekindled Hu's anger. Stamping his foot, Hu declared, “Very well! I shall open one and show him.” Liu Bucai was ordered to make the preparations and set off that very day for Zhili to buy medicinal ingredients. Along with them, he brought back several hundred dogskin plasters for Hu to try.

zh: 这“狗皮膏药”是“房中药”的一种。刘不才在采买药材时，由于他的豪爽风趣，结识了好些朋友，酒酣耳热之际，少不得谈谈风月。其中有个苏州人，谈起上一科的状元，现任河北学政的洪钧，说他最近写信回苏州，托人买妾，信中说得很坦率，娶妾无非及时行乐，用不着找什么理由，没有儿子，一定说是“不孝有三，无后为大”，单身在外，说是没有人照料起居，这些话、无非自欺欺人而已。他说：及时行乐，这句话，要分做两面来谈，一面是及时，娶妾就要娶得早，人到中年，渐形衰颓，美色当前，力不从心，不但自误，而且误人，一面是行乐，当然要娶美妾，才有乐趣而言。大家听他说得诚恳，亦以诚恳相待，终于替他觅到了一个上海的名妓，国色天香的赛金花作妾。于是另有一人感叹：说少年创业，精力过人，就是没有钱，及至创业已成，钱是有了，精力却嫌不足，姬妾满眼，广田自荒，说不定还会戴上绿帽子，人生憾事，莫过于此。这些话提醒了刘不才，想起胡雪岩或许亦有此憾。因而打听，有没有好春药，只壮阳，不伤身。当时便有人指点，北京鼓楼有一家小药店，可以买到外用的“狗皮膏药”，药性王道，不似内服的春药，竭泽而渔那样霸道。不过这家小药店的主人，颇以制售此药为耻，须有跟他交情很深的人介绍，而且只特制，不零售。刘不才的人缘不错，居然找到了适当的介绍人，出重金订制了一批。胡雪岩试用之下，床第之间，便就此放纵了。
en: These dogskin plasters were a kind of sexual stimulant. While buying medicines, Liu's generosity and humour had won him many friends. Over wine, their conversation inevitably turned to women. One man from Suzhou mentioned Hong Jun, the top graduate of the previous imperial examination and now Education Commissioner of Hebei. Hong had recently written home asking someone to find him a concubine. His letter was frank: the purpose of taking a concubine was to enjoy life while one could. There was no need for excuses such as “Of the three failures in filial duty, having no heir is the greatest,” when a man lacked a son, or “There is no one to look after me,” when he lived away from home. Such claims merely deceived oneself and others. Enjoying life while one could, he said, had two sides. First, one must be timely: take a concubine early, for by middle age strength begins to decline. To face beauty with insufficient vigour was to disappoint not only oneself but another person. Second came enjoyment, which naturally required a beautiful concubine. His listeners responded to such frankness with equal sincerity and eventually found him a celebrated Shanghai courtesan of exceptional beauty, Sai Jinhua. Another man lamented that in youth, while building a career, one had ample energy but no money. Once established, one had money but insufficient energy: concubines everywhere, broad fields lying untilled, and perhaps the risk of being cuckolded. What greater regret could life offer? This reminded Liu that Hu might feel the same. He asked whether there was a good aphrodisiac that strengthened virility without harming the body. Someone directed him to a small medicine shop near Beijing's Drum Tower. It sold externally applied dogskin plasters, said to act gently, unlike internal stimulants that exhausted a man like draining a pond to catch its fish. The proprietor, however, was ashamed of making and selling them. A close friend's introduction was required, and they were prepared only to order, never sold over the counter. Liu's popularity enabled him to find a suitable intermediary. He paid heavily for a batch. After trying them, Hu gave free rein to himself in bed.

zh: “这是没法子的事。”七姑奶奶说：“除非你想得开，”这意思是，螺蛳太太可能容许胡雪岩另外纳妾来分她的宠？她心里想，自己是半正半侧的身分，老太太固然宠信有加，大太太也能相安无事，但做当家人难免为下人憎厌，倘或娶进一房夷太太来。为人厉害，又为下人撺掇，联络大太太，不顾先进门为大“这个规矩，明枪暗箭，处处作对，虽不见得怕她，但免不了常常生气，这却是不可不虑的事。正在沉吟之时：七姑奶奶又开口了：“去年秋天，应春生了一场伤寒，病好调养。不能出门，在家也实在无聊不过，请了个说书的，出堂会，来解闷，每天下半天两个钟头，说的一部书叫做《儿女英雄传》讲女人家吃醋，实在有点道理。”“喔！”螺蛳太太问道：“说书的怎么说？”“他说：吃醋分会吃、不会吃两种，每种又分三等。不会吃醋的，吃得可笑、可怜、可怕，譬如……”“七姐，”螺蛳太太打断她的话说：“不会吃的，就不要去谈它了。”“好，讲会吃的，也分三等，叫做常品，能品、神品。常品，也不必谈，先说能品，譬如说象你，一等一的人材，小爷叔再娶了一个来，就算能胜过你，只要你宽宏大量，声色不动，而且照样处处关心小爷叔的饮食起居，他心里存了个亏欠你的心，依旧是你得宠。这就是会吃醋的能品。”
en: “There is no remedy,” the Seventh Lady said, “unless you can accept the situation generously.” She meant: could Madam Luosi allow Hu to take another concubine and share his favour? Madam Luosi considered her position, halfway between principal wife and concubine. The old lady trusted and favoured her, and she lived peacefully with the principal wife, but managing the household inevitably earned servants' resentment. Suppose a formidable new concubine arrived and, egged on by servants, allied herself with the principal wife, disregarding the rule that earlier entry conferred seniority and opposing her openly and covertly at every turn. She might not be afraid, but she would constantly be angry. That danger could not be ignored. As she reflected, the Seventh Lady spoke again. “Last autumn Yingchun had a fever. During his convalescence he couldn't go out and was dreadfully bored, so we hired a storyteller to perform at home for two hours every afternoon. The book was Tales of Heroic Sons and Daughters. Its account of women's jealousy made considerable sense.” “What did the storyteller say?” “He divided jealous women into those who manage jealousy well and those who don't, with three grades in each. Those who don't are laughable, pitiable or terrifying. For example…” “Never mind those who don't,” Madam Luosi interrupted. “Very well. Those who manage it well are also divided into three grades: ordinary, skilful and divine. We can leave out the ordinary. Take the skilful. A first-rate woman like you might see Little Uncle marry someone who surpassed even you. Yet if you remained generous, showed no disturbance and cared as attentively as ever for his food and daily comforts, he would feel indebted to you and you would retain his favour. That is skilful jealousy.”

zh: 螺蛳太太在想，照此说来，大太太就是个能品。只不知神品以是如何？心里转着念头，口中便问了出来。“你问神品，说穿了也没有啥稀奇，象你这样能干，做起来也不费事，一句话，恩威并用！她安分守己，是好的，你比小爷叔还要宠她，她有不守规矩的地方，你尽管说她、管她。将来有了儿女，你比她生母还要知痛痒，还要会教训。那一来，上上下下哪个不服你？哪个不说你贤惠？这样子吃醋，真吃得神了！”七姑奶奶的话，句句打入螺蛳太太心坎，而且别有领会。如今一家的主人，第一是“老太太”，第二是“老爷”，第三是“太太”，第四才轮到她，除了下人，只有管她的，而没有她管的。倘或亲自经手挑选，替胡雪岩多娶几房姨太太，照七姑奶奶所说的，拿“恩威并用”四个字来调教，叫她们心服口服，那时才真正显得出当家人的威风气派。这样想着，不自觉地在脸上绽开了笑容。七姑奶奶便也笑道：“怎么样？四姐，你也想吃一吃这种看不出来是吃醋的醋？““只伯我不会吃。”螺蛳太太说：“七姐，你也帮我留意留意。”一听这话，七姑奶奶知道她决心照她的话去做了。本来是闲谈，即令有为她策划的意思，亦需从长计议，不道她从善如流，立刻就听信了！实在出人意外。
en: By that account, Madam Luosi thought, the principal wife belonged to the skilful grade. What, then, was the divine? She asked aloud. “Nothing particularly extraordinary, once explained. With your ability, it would not be difficult. In a word, combine kindness with authority. If she behaves properly, treat her well; cherish her even more than Little Uncle does. If she breaks the rules, speak to her and keep her in order. When she has children, understand their needs better than their own mother and be better at bringing them up. Then who in the whole household will not respect you? Who will not call you virtuous? That is truly divine jealousy.” Every word went straight to Madam Luosi's heart, and she saw a further implication. In the household hierarchy, the old lady came first, the master second, the principal wife third, and she herself only fourth. Apart from the servants, there were people to govern her but nobody for her to govern. If she personally selected several more concubines for Hu and trained them through kindness and authority until they sincerely acknowledged her, she would at last display the full dignity and power of the household's manager. A smile appeared on her face without her noticing. The Seventh Lady smiled too. “Well, Sister Luo? Would you like to practise this jealousy that does not look like jealousy?” “I only fear I may not know how. Keep an eye out for someone for me, Seventh Sister.” The Seventh Lady realized that she had decided to act on the advice. It had begun as casual conversation; even if meant as a plan, it would require long consideration. She had never expected such immediate acceptance.

zh: 转念到此，她顿感肩头沉更，俗语说的“若要家不和，娶个小老婆”，象螺蛳太太这样的情形，实在少而又少，再说罗四姐是胡雪岩自己看中的，即令进门以后不如意，也怪不到她头上。现在不同了，竞完全象是她出的主意，将来倘有风波，从胡老太太起，都会怨她。因而不能不好好替螺蛳太太想一想。“四姐，”她想到就说：“凡事想得蛮好，做起来不太容易。小爷叔如果要讨堂子里的人，你不可以许他，堂子里的人有习气，难管。”“是的。要讨总要讨好人家的女儿。”螺蛳太太又说：“我要先同大先生说明白，他尽管自己去物色，人一定要让我看过。”她紧接着又说，“其实用不着他自己去物色，我先托人替他去挑。”螺蛳太太说到做到，三、四年工夫，陆续物色，加上胡雪岩自己选中的，一共娶了十一房姨太太，连她自己在内，恰好凑成十二金钗之数。
en: At that thought, the Seventh Lady suddenly felt a weight on her shoulders. As the saying went, “If you want discord at home, take a concubine.” Women like Madam Luosi were exceedingly rare. Besides, Hu had chosen Luo for himself. Even if things had gone badly after she entered the household, the Seventh Lady could not have been blamed. This was different: it now seemed entirely her proposal. If trouble followed, everyone, beginning with Old Madam Hu, would resent her. She must therefore think carefully on her friend's behalf. “Sister Luo, things sound fine in the planning but are not so easy to carry out. If Little Uncle wants to marry someone from a courtesan house, you must refuse. Such women have habits that make them difficult to manage.” “Yes. She must be a girl from a respectable family. I shall make it clear to him first: he may look for someone himself, but I must see her. In fact, there is no need for him to look. I shall ask people to choose someone for him.” She did as she said. Over three or four years, the women she found, together with those Hu chose himself, made eleven additional concubines. Including her, they numbered exactly twelve, like the Twelve Beauties of the novel.

zh: 眷属一多，又加上生意发达，不断添人，原有的房子虽然一再扩充，始终不敷所需，到后来基地所限，倘非彻底翻造，就得另辟新居。胡雪岩便与螺蛳太大商量，打算另外觅地建一所住宅，将他的两个胞弟，连同各式办事人等一起迁了出去，空出来的房子拆掉，改做花园，另外要造一座“走马楼”，将“十二金钡”集中一起。螺蛳太太对造一座走马楼，倒颇赞成，但对另建新宅却有异议。“请二老爷、三老爷搬出去，会伤老太太的心，亲戚也会说闲话。这件事，老爷还要斟酌。”听说会伤老母之心，胡雪岩立即打消了原议，不过，“房子不够住，总要想法子。”他问：“你有啥好主意？”“我听说间壁刘家的房子要卖，后门口米店老板死掉了，两个儿子分家争产，米店归哪个管，一直在吵，也想卖了房子分现款。不如拿这两家的地皮买过来，打通围墙，不是可以联在一起？”这下又激起了胡雪岩好摆排场的意兴。恰好这年丝价大涨。胡雪岩操纵“洋庄”，结算下来三个月的工夫，赚了四十万银子，‘决定大治园林。“譬如我没有挣到这笔款子，”他这样对螺蛳太太说：“我照你的意思来做，不过范围要做得大，前后左右都要临街，方方整整一大片，象王府的气派才好。”这是有面子的事，螺蛳太太当然高兴。于是胡雪岩派人到周围人家去游说，动以厚利，其中除了两家，都愿意迁让。
en: With more family members and an expanding business continually bringing new personnel, the house proved inadequate despite repeated extensions. Eventually the limits of the site meant either complete rebuilding or finding another home. Hu discussed it with Madam Luosi. He proposed buying land and building a new residence elsewhere, moving his two younger brothers there along with the various people who worked for him, and demolishing the vacated buildings to make a garden. He also wanted a gallery-lined residence where his Twelve Beauties could live together. Madam Luosi approved of the latter but objected to the separate house. “Asking Second Master and Third Master to move out will hurt your mother. The relatives will gossip too. You ought to reconsider.” At the thought of hurting his mother, Hu abandoned the proposal at once. “But there isn't enough room. We must do something. Have you a better idea?” “I hear the Liu house next door is for sale. The owner of the rice shop behind us has died, and his two sons keep quarrelling over the division of the estate and who should run the shop. They also want to sell the building and divide the cash. Why not buy both properties and break through the walls to join them to ours?” This revived Hu's appetite for grand display. Silk prices happened to rise sharply that year. Through his control of the silk trade with foreign houses, he made four hundred thousand taels in three months. He decided on a grand garden. “Let us pretend I never earned that money. I shall follow your suggestion, but on a larger scale. Streets must bound it on all four sides, making one great, regular block, with the grandeur of a prince's mansion.” Madam Luosi was naturally pleased by such distinction. Hu sent men to persuade the surrounding households, offering substantial inducements. All but two agreed to move and sell.

zh: 这两家一家是酒栈，说存酒搬运不便，无法出让，态度虽然坚决，说话却很客气。另一家就不同了。这一家是个极小的剃头店，位置恰好在元宝街与望仙桥直街转角之处，为出入所必经，整片房子，在此交通要道上缺了一块，而且是家破破烂烂的剃头店，就象绝色美人，瞎了一只眼那样令人难以忍受。“好是啥意思？”胡雪岩说：“她如果想卖好价钱，尽管说。要多少就多少好了。”她，是指剃头店的“崔老太婆”。老板是她的儿子，脾气虽然也很犟，但经不住胡家人三天两头去说好话，又看在钱的分上。意思倒有些活动了。
en: One holdout was a wine warehouse. It said the stored wine was too difficult to move and refused to sell, firmly but politely. The other was different. It was a tiny barbershop at the corner of Yuanbao Street and Wangxianqiao Straight Street, a place everyone had to pass when entering or leaving. To have a gap in the estate at such an important junction—and a dilapidated barbershop at that—was as intolerable as a peerless beauty with one eye blind. “What does she want?” Hu demanded. “If she wants a good price, let her name it. Whatever she asks, she can have.” “She” was Old Mrs Cui, the proprietor's mother. Her son was stubborn too, but the Hu household's frequent visits and courteous persuasion, together with the prospect of money, had begun to move him.

zh: 可是崔老大婆执意不允，原来她是年轻守寡，孤苦无依，好不容易将儿子抚养成人，也只是个剃头匠，她不怨自己当初不该叫儿子去学了这一行，只说老天无眼，慢慢养成了乖僻的脾气，最恨有钱人，越有钱越恨。因此，胡雪岩说到“要多少就多少”这句话，恰恰犯了她的忌。“你同你们东家去说，他是财神，我们是穷鬼，打不上交道。他发财是他的，他又不是阎王、判官，我也用不着怕他。”去打交道的是胡雪岩门下的一个清客，名叫张子洪，以脾气好出名，此时也忍不住生气，说了一句：“他虽不是阎王判官，不过是个道台。”“道台莫非不讲王法？”崔老太婆答说：“我们娘儿两个两条命，随便他好了。”这番话传到胡雪岩耳朵里，气得一天没有吃饭。门下清客，帐房、管事，还有听差打杂的，议论纷纷，而且出了好些主意，有的说请县里的差役来跟她说话，有的说放火烧掉她的房子再说，有的说造张假契约跟她打官司，但胡雪岩终觉不忍，螺蛳太太也怕逼出人命案子来，约束下人，不准胡来。以至于一直到巨宅落成，元室街也重新翻修过，那家剃头店始终存在。
en: His mother, however, refused absolutely. Widowed young and left without support, she had struggled to bring him up, only to see him become a barber. Rather than blame herself for choosing that trade for him, she accused Heaven of blindness. Over time she had grown contrary and bitter, hating the wealthy in proportion to their wealth. Hu's promise to pay whatever she asked touched precisely her sore point. “Tell your employer that he may be the God of Wealth, but we are paupers. We have no dealings with him. Let him make his fortune. He is neither the King of Hell nor a judge in the underworld. I have no reason to fear him.” The negotiator was Zhang Zihong, a literary hanger-on in Hu's household, famous for his mild temper. Even he lost patience. “He may not be the King of Hell or an underworld judge, but he is a circuit intendant.” “Does that put him above the law? My son and I have only our two lives. Let him do as he pleases.” When Hu heard this, he was so angry that he ate nothing all day. His household retainers, accountants, managers and servants proposed all kinds of measures: send the county bailiffs, burn down the house, or forge a deed and sue her. Hu could not bring himself to do it. Madam Luosi also feared that coercion might lead to a death and restrained the servants from any rash act. Even after the great mansion was completed and Yuanbao Street repaved, the barbershop remained.

zh: 落成之日，大宴宾客，共分三日，第一天是“三大宪”，杭州府、仁和、钱塘两县，以及候补道，邀约在籍的绅士作陪，入席之前，主人亲自引导游园，曲曲折折，转过假山，只见东南方树木掩映之中，矗起一座高楼，华丽非凡，令人不解的是，四周雕栏，金光闪耀，远远望去，谁也猜不透是何缘故。“雪翁，”巡抚杨昌浚问道：“那是个什么所在？”“是内人所住的一座楼。”听说是内眷住处，杨昌浚不便再间，私下打听，才知道那座楼名为“百狮楼”。栏杆柱子上，用紫檀打磨出一百个狮子，突出的狮目，是用黄金铸就，所以映日耀眼，令人不可逼视。“太太们住的地方，怎么叫百狮楼，莫非‘河东狮吼’这句话，他都不懂。”“不是。因为那位太太称为螺蛳太太，所以胡大先生造了这座楼给她住。”杨昌浚再问“螺蛳太太”之名如何而起，是何出身。打听清楚了觉得未免过分，便悄悄写了一封信给在肃州的左宗棠，颇有微词。
en: The completion was celebrated with three days of banquets. On the first day, the guests were the three principal provincial authorities, the prefect of Hangzhou, the magistrates of Renhe and Qiantang, and expectant circuit intendants, with local gentry invited to keep them company. Before the meal, Hu personally led them through the garden. Following its winding paths around a rockery, they saw an extraordinarily splendid tower rising among the trees to the southeast. What puzzled them was the gold light flashing from the carved railings all around it. At that distance, nobody could account for it. “Mr Hu,” Governor Yang Changjun asked, “what is that building?” “The residence of my wife.” Hearing that it belonged to the women's quarters, Yang could not inquire further, but private questions brought the explanation. It was called the Hundred Lions Tower. One hundred lions carved and polished from zitan stood on the railing posts. Their protruding eyes were cast in gold and glittered in the sunlight so brightly that one could scarcely look at them. “Why call the ladies' residence Hundred Lions Tower? Does he not know the saying about the lioness of Hedong roaring?” “No, that isn't it. The lady is called Madam Luosi, and he built the tower for her.” Yang asked how she had acquired the name and what her origins were. Once informed, he felt that Hu had gone rather too far and quietly wrote to Zuo at Suzhou in Gansu, expressing some criticism.

zh: 哪知左宗棠对他的看法，颇不以为然，只是不便明言，恰巧他的长子来信，亦批评了胡雪岩，正好借题发挥，说一个人的享用，求其相称，胡雪岩的功劳，世人不尽了解，他很清楚，西征军事之能有今日，全亏得有胡雪岩，享用稍过，自可无愧。他又提到他的儿女亲家，也是平生第一知己的陶澍，在两江总督任上时，他的女婿胡林翼，以翰林在江宁闲住，每天选歌征色，花的都是老丈人的“养廉银”，内帐房有一次向陶演表示，胡林翼挥霍无度，是否应该稍加节制？陶澎告诉他说：“尽管让他花！他将来要为国家出力，有钱亦没有工夫去花。”胡雪岩跟胡林翼的情形虽有不同，但个人的享用，比起为国家所谋的大利来，即令豪奢亦不足道。这些活辗转传到浙江，胡雪岩感激在心，对左宗棠自然越发尽忠竭力，但螺狮太太却心生警惕，与七姑奶奶私下谈起来，都认为“树大招风”，应该要收敛了。可是胡雪岩只问一句：“怎么收法？”螺蛳太太却又无词以对。因为胡雪岩所凭借的是信用，信用是建立在大家对他的信心上面，而信心是由胡雪岩的场面造成的。场面只能大，不能小，否则只要有人无意间说一句：“胡大先生如今也不比从前了。”立刻就会惹起无数猜测，原来有仇恨的、无怨无仇只是由于妒嫉的，都将推波助澜，大放谣言，那一来信用就要动摇，后果不堪设想。
en: Zuo disagreed considerably with Yang but could not conveniently say so outright. As it happened, his eldest son also wrote to criticize Hu, giving him a suitable occasion to express his view. A man's enjoyments, he said, should be proportionate to his deserts. The world did not fully understand Hu's services, but he did. The western campaign owed its present success entirely to Hu; a little excess in his pleasures need give him no shame. He cited Tao Shu, his closest lifelong friend and the father of his child's spouse. When Tao was Governor-General of Liangjiang, his son-in-law Hu Linyi, a Hanlin academician living idly at Jiangning, spent his days seeking singers and beautiful women, all at the expense of his father-in-law's integrity allowance. Once Tao's household accountant asked whether Hu Linyi's extravagance ought to be restrained. “Let him spend,” Tao replied. “He will serve the country one day. Then, even if he has money, he will have no time to spend it.” Hu Xueyan's circumstances differed, but compared with the great benefits he secured for the country, even extravagant personal pleasures counted for little. These remarks eventually reached Zhejiang. Deeply grateful, Hu served Zuo with still greater loyalty and effort. Madam Luosi, however, grew uneasy. In private talks with the Seventh Lady, both agreed that a tall tree catches the wind: it was time to become less conspicuous. Yet Hu needed only to ask, “How are we to cut back?” and she had no answer. For Hu depended on credit; credit rested on the confidence others placed in him; and that confidence was created by the grandeur of his establishment. The display could only grow, never shrink. Otherwise, a single casual remark—“Mr Hu is no longer what he used to be”—would instantly set off endless speculation. Those who bore him grudges, and those who had no grievance but were merely envious, would fan the rumours. His credit would be shaken, with consequences too terrible to contemplate.
